subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: The linked bug fix and the strict-validation PR encode opposite product contracts, and the choice affects existing scheduled jobs, upgrade behavior, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Choose one-shot-only rejection
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after documenting caller behavior and user recovery.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the default only for newly created jobs and explicitly document that existing implicit jobs require operator action or a later migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but require a path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron normalization, SQLite store migration/default semantics, and product compatibility, where steipete has the strongest recent history.
